 Looking for things to do this weekend in Singapore? Indulge in the spread of events and experiences we’ve curated for you.
 Photo: Courtesy of Fujiko and Singapore International Film Festival By  Harper's BAZAAR Singapore  -  published 21 Oct 2026 
 Our island may be small, but there’s always plenty to look forward to. Shut your laptop for the weekend and see our roundup of the most exciting events happening now, from pop-up markets featuring viral lifestyle brands and buzzy collaborations to must-see exhibitions and food festivals.
 Stay tuned to our curation of things to do this weekend, updated weekly.

 Singapore International Film Festival
 A still from Fujiko .
 Photo: Courtesy of Fujiko and Singapore International Film Festival Singapore International Film Festival is back for its 37th edition, and there’s plenty to look forward to if you’re a film buff. Over the course of 10 days, catch new films from around the region, Mexico and Belgium; rediscover celebrated movies like Lagaan ; and join in on dialogues with award-winning filmmakers and actors like Aamir Khan ( 3 Idiots ), Kiko Mizuhara ( Attack on Titan and Helter Skelter ) and Shim Eun Kyung ( The Killers and Sunny ).
 Looking for film recommendations? This weekend, see Orang Minyak , a buzzy horror flick featuring the titular folklore entity, or catch the Singapore premiere of Fujiko , a Japanese film that follows a young disco dancer as she navigates society as a single mother.
 Singapore International Film Festival runs from now to 1 November 2026 across various locations. For the full list of programmes and more information, visit Singapore International Film Festival’s site . 
 Home | ground
 This Saturday, Goodman Arts Centre is turning into a space to gather, connect and create. Join SOTA and LASALLE alumni, as well as past and present tenants of Goodman Arts Centre as they bring you a series of unique activities, performances and exhibitions.
 Textile artist Nicole Goh shares how you can properly press a school uniform or a dress shirt while she delves deeper into materials and memories associated with them. Sit for a quiet round of tea with visual artist Adeline Kueh and be invited to make meaningful conversation, discovering first-hand how stories and artistic ideas can appear around a table.
 Tapping on the space’s past as home to Tun Seri Lanang Malay Secondary School , you’ll also be able to shape a little companion out of paper clips, noteboook paper and post-its to carry with you for the day.
 Home | ground is happening on 24 October 2026 at Goodman Arts Centre, 90 Goodman Road, from 4 to 10pm. For more information, visit Arts House Group’s site. 
 Toy Story x Peaceminusone: The First Fan
 Photo: Courtesy of Mighty Jaxx Joining the Bigbang hype train in Singapore is the exhibition and pop-up store by Toy Story and G-Dragon ’s Peaceminusone . Here, your first loves and your favourite idol meet through a series of adorable keychains, reusable stickers, drink cups and more that feature the Toy Story characters and Peaceminusone’s famous daisy motif. For the fashion conscious VIPs, there are also T-shirts, caps, wallet chains and scarves that feature a more minimalistic design.
 While the pieces above are available for online order, there are eight pop-up exclusives that may just make the trip worthwhile. Think: a graphic tee, caps in four colours and tote bags in three different designs.
 Toy Story x Peaceminusone: The First Fan runs from 16 October to 11 November 2026 at CQ @ Clarke Quay, 3 River Valley Road, from 1 to 11pm daily. Entry is ticketed, purchase your ticket here . For more information, visit The First Fan’s site. 
 QORE: Circularity at the Core
 Thailand-based design platform and circular-material manufacturer QORE is partnering with Alchemist for a month-long pop-up that will see a showcase, exclusive stool designs in limited quantities and a craft workshop. Across Alchemist’s three-level space, see how industrial waste and coffee chaff alike can be repurposed into functional objects like furniture. Here, you’ll be able to get your hands on one of 119 QORE × Alchemist Betterism Stools, a sleek, Singapore-exclusive made from discarded materials.
 Photo: Courtesy of Alchemist If you’re there on a Saturday, take part in a planter workshop hosted by Soilboy . See a filter coffee brewing showcase, learn how to care for and repot plants, and take home one in a collaboration-exclusive Coffee Waste Planter.
 QORE: Circularity at the Core runs from now to 31 October 2026, Alchemist Arab Street, 119 Arab Street, from 9am to 6pm daily. Sign up for the Coffee & Plant Care Workshop here, and find more information, visit Alchemist’s page . 
 “Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism and the Silk Road”
 Photo: Courtesy of Dunhuang Academy ICYMI, there’s a new exhibition at the Asian Civilisations Museum that everyone’s been talking about. Titled “Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism and the Silk Road”, the showcase revisits the storied history of Dunhuang, a city in northwest China connected to India and the Middle East that played a vital role in trade, religion and cultural exchanges in ancient times. 
 For this exhibition, the first of its kind in Southeast Asia, ACM collaborated with Dunhuang Academy to bring life-sized replicas and original artwork from the Mogao Caves. See how life was really like more than a thousand years ago with sculptures and paintings from the Tang and Sui dynasties without needing to travel to the edge of the Gobi desert.
 “Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism and the Silk Road” runs from now to 7 March 2027 at Asian Civilisations Museum, 1 Empress Place, from 10am to 7pm Sundays to Thursdays and 10am to 9pm on Fridays. For more information, visit ACM’s site.   
 Café Mademoiselle
 Photo: Courtesy of PS. Cafe You’re in for a sensory experience at Chanel ’s collab with PS.Cafe . The exclusive menu is inspired by the brand’s newest fragrance, the ambery-woody Coco Mademoiselle Crush Absolu, translating the perfume’s key notes like grapefruit, rose, jasmine and vanilla into a lineup of dishes.
 Try the saffron chicken tartine, which has pink grapefruit, or the earl grey pancake “exotique”, mousse au chocolat noir and rose lychee crush for something sweet. If a midday pick-me-up is what you need, the menu also has as a bergamot latte, served hot or iced, for a caffeine boost.
 PS.Cafe’s ‘Café Mademoiselle’ menu will be available from now to 31 October, from Monday to Friday, 11am to 10pm to Saturday and Sunday, 10am to 10pm, at PS.Cafe One Fullerton and PS.Cafe Palais Renaissance. For more information, visit  PS.Cafe’s Instagram .

 teamLab: Infinite Existence
 teamLab,  Lotus Elephant  © teamLab
 Photo: Courtesy of Ikkan Art LLC International art collective teamLab is in town for its first solo exhibit at Supper House . The showcase will see eight monitor-based works inspired by the visual language of premodern East Asian paintings, which combines multiple viewpoints, shifting perspectives and time periods into a single image.
 Here, teamLab expands on their concept of “Ultrasubjective Space”, which subverts the Western practice of featuring a single, fixed subject in their art. This exhibition in particular offers viewers and quieter and more contemplative look at teamLab’s work.
 You’ll see digital installations including “Continuous Life and Death at the Now of Eternity II”, which explores the cycle of life and death through flowers that emerge, change and disappear as the day progresses; and “Universe of Water Particles – Gold”, a virtual waterfall of cascading water particles, among others.
 teamLab: Infinite Existence runs from now to 8 November 2026 at #04-02, Supper House, Tanjong Pagar Distripark, 37 Keppel Road, from 12 to 7pm Thursdays to Saturdays and 12 to 5pm on Sundays. For more information, visit Supper House’s site. 
 Birkenstock Walk Naturally
 Photo: Courtesy of Birkenstock More screen time, more problems. If you’re looking to disconnect for a couple of hours, Birkenstock is hosting a whole series of fun events across New Bahru for the community. They’ve taken over the famous slide on the lawn and collaborated with stores like Crafune, Make by Ginlee and Soilboy for exclusive merch like bag charms featuring silhouettes from the German footwear brand and even your very own sustainable mini planter.
You can also pop by Off Duty Pilates for a quick workout sesh, then head to Atipico to taste an exclusive menu featuring toasted focaccia with mirin-glazed mushrooms and brioche filled with vanilla cream. Or, try one of their two drinks: a berry yuzu soda and a banana and mango shake blended with coconut milk.
Our tip? Stop at the kiosk out front if you’re rocking your Birks—you’ll get to redeem a complimentary coffee from PPP Coffee , while stocks last. We also hear that there’ll be a few more exciting pop-ups to come over the month, so keep your eyes peeled.
 Coming up soon is Walk With The Pack, a collaboration between Birkenstock and Pop Pop Pet that will take you and your furry friend on a stroll around the New Bahru neighbourhood and the Singapore river.
 Birkenstock Walk Naturally runs from now to 26 October 2026 at New Bahru, 46 Kim Yam Road, from 9am to 8pm Sundays to Thursdays and 9am to 9pm Fridays and Saturdays. The event is open to all, but selected experiences require advance registration. Walk With The Pack is happening on 24 October 2026, from 5pm to 7pm, and you can register and find more details here . For more information, visit Birkenstock’s site . 
 The Story of Studio Ghibli
 Photo: Courtesy of Studio Ghibli Further out on the horizon, but worth flagging now, is the world premiere of The Story of Studio Ghibli at Gardens by the Bay this December. Spanning nearly 3,500 square metres, it will be the first time an exhibition of this scale dedicated to the storied Japanese animation studio has opened anywhere in the world, with Singapore given the honour of hosting its debut.
 The show promises 12 fully realised environments, each drawing from a different corner of the Ghibli universe. From the pastoral wonder of My Neighbor Totoro to the eerie, bathhouse-bound world of Spirited Away , the coming-of-age charm of Kiki's Delivery Service , and the environmental gravity of Princess Mononoke .
 For a studio whose visual language has become genuinely iconic, and instantly recognisable even to those who've never seen the films, the promise of walking through these worlds physically, rather than watching them on screen, is a significant one.
 The Story Of Studio Ghibli runs from 18 December 2026 to 4 July 2027 at West Lawn, Gardens by the Bay, 18 Marina Drive. Book an early bird ticket on Klook here .

 “Singapore Odyssea: A Journey Through Time”
 Photo: Courtesy of National Museum of Singapore “Singapore Odyssea: A Journey Through Time”, a permanent exhibition staged at National Museum of Singapore, encourages visitors to voyage into Singapore’s 700 years of history, hinging on the sea as a key player to our island’s transformation over the years.
 The showcase happens over five chapters, opening with a ‘time-travelling’ vessel that offers a glimpse of Singapore in the future, before taking guests back in time to see pivotal points in Singapore’s history. Descend the ramp and see moments from Singapore’s first National Day Parade, early nation-building efforts and our mythical past along the way, all told from the perspective of the sea.
 More magic awaits at the base of the Glass Rotunda. Step through a towering digital waterfall to find more scenes from the past, and tap your RFID bracelet against a ‘well’ to release your adopted magical companion into the ocean.
 “Singapore Odyssea: A Journey Through Time” runs daily from 10am to 6pm. Book a slot here and find more information on National Museum of Singapore’s website .

 Singapore Stories: ​Pathways and Detours in Art
 Photo: Courtesy of National Gallery Singapore “Singapore Stories: Pathways and Detours in Art” is a long-term exhibition at `National Gallery Singapore. The first part explores Singapore’s stories and societal changes through art from the 19th century to the 1960s. Featuring over 200 artworks and artefacts across four sections, the exhibition showcases how artists such as Georgette Chen , Liu Kang , Annaratnam Gunaratnam , P. Ramlee , have experimented with medium and expression while addressing themes like colonialism, urban change, and globalisation.
